title: Green Spaces, Safety Linked to Better Sleep — Study
paragraphs: Getting a good night's sleep is important for our health. Poor sleep is linked to heart disease, obesity and depression. Now, a new study from Japan suggests that the way our neighborhood looks may affect how well we sleep.

The study was carried out by researchers at Osaka Metropolitan University. It involved 1,089 working adults aged between 40 and 59 who lived on the third floor or lower of apartment buildings in Tokyo. The participants answered questions about their sleep and how safe they felt in their neighborhoods.

To study the neighborhoods, the researchers used artificial intelligence (AI) to look at more than 200,000 images from Google Street View. The AI identified different features of the streets, such as trees, buildings and sidewalks.

The researchers found that people who lived in greener neighborhoods, and on streets that were surrounded by buildings or trees, tended to sleep longer and have fewer problems falling or staying asleep.

The researchers believe that feeling safe may partly explain this link. Green streets were linked to people feeling that their neighborhoods were safer and more lively. In turn, people who felt safer tended to sleep longer.
Surprisingly, streets that were designed to be good for walking, with more sidewalks and traffic signs, were linked to people feeling less safe and sleeping less.

However, the study only shows a link. It does not prove that the design of a neighborhood directly affects sleep. Also, the participants reported their own sleep, which may not always be accurate. In addition, the study only included a specific group of people in Tokyo.
Other research has found similar results. For example, a 2024 study in 18 countries found that people living on greener streets tended to sleep better.
The researchers hope their findings will help city planners design neighborhoods that are better for health.
